text.p: These are the highlights of the main Sao Paulo and Rio de Janeiro newspapers this moorning.
Industry is optimistic consumers will continue to buy more value-added goods this year because they can pay in instalments.
Brazil's January trade balance posted a deficit of $413 million including $534 million in oil imports by state oil giant Petrobras.
-- HEALTH MINISTRY MIGHT DELAY CONDOM HANDOUTS
The Health Ministry has been slow in delivering a total of 2.7 million condoms to state governments and non-governmental organizations so they can hand them out during this year's carnival.
The government is preparing a campaign to win support for constitutional reforms which are on the agenda this year.
-- CARDOSO SEES NO MORE DOUBTS ABOUT CVRD SALE
President Fernando Henrique Cardoso said all doubts regarding the privatization rules for state mining firm CVRD had been removed and national sovereignty was not at risk with the company's sell-off.
-- TRADE BALANCE CREATES RIFT BETWEEN GOVT AND PETROBRAS
The government and state oil monopoly Petrobras are blaming each other for the problems with January's trade figures which initially failed to include the correct number of oil imports.
-- Reuters has not verified the stories and cannot vouch for their accuracy.
-- Simona de Logu, Rio de Janeiro newsroom, 5521 507 4151
